cards.title: DATAWEAVER: Authoring Data-Driven Narratives through the Integrated Composition of Visualization and Text
cards.relevant_page_map: motivation (PDF pp. 1, 3); interface (PDF pp. 4–7); evaluation (PDF pp. 8–9); limitations (PDF pp. 9–10).

quotes: "Author’s Accepted Version. Published in Computer Graphics Forum. Final version available at: https://doi.org/10.1111/cgf.70098" (p. 1)
"DATAWEAVER: Authoring Data-Driven Narratives through the Integrated Composition of Visualization and Text" (p. 1)

identity_entries.value: motivation (PDF pp. 1, 3); interface (PDF pp. 4–7); evaluation (PDF pp. 8–9); limitations (PDF pp. 9–10).
quotes: "Despite its potential, authoring data-driven stories poses an interdisciplinary challenge, requiring a combination of skills in data analysis, visualization, and narrative writing [RHDC18, LRIC15]." (p. 1)
"Our work aims to help streamline this process by integrating visualization and text authoring into a cohesive workflow." (p. 3)
"We developed a preliminary Callout Taxonomy (Table 1) as a theoretical guidance for more relevant data facts generation and their effective organization." (p. 4)

"The interface comprises three major components: a flow-based Authoring Canvas (Figure 2-A) for composing visualizations and text, an Insight Cart (Figure 2-B) for managing insights, and a Review Page (Figure 2-C) for refining the story and previewing the final visual data narrative in multiple formats." (p. 5)

"The vis-to-text composition starts with a created visualization and follows an interact-compute-select-generate-revise workflow with users, algorithms, and LLM collaboratively handle respective steps:" (p. 6)
"DATAWEAVER utilizes LLMs to understand and infer contextually relevant information, enabling authors to expand their narratives using relevant information from the data." (p. 7)

"To evaluate the effectiveness and usability of DATAWEAVER and gather valuable feedback, we conducted a two-part evaluation: a focused user study, followed by a longitudinal week-long diary study." (p. 8)
"Text-to-vis composition showed promise but also exhibited inconsistent performance due to data limitation." (p. 9)
"Another key limitation of DATAWEAVER is its primary focus on assembling together data facts while lacking support for higher-level storylines." (p. 10)

rq3_entries.value: computation and ranking of candidate facts, fact-constrained narrative drafting, interpretation of selected prose, chart recommendation, and visualization-specification generation (PDF pp. 6–7).
quotes: "S2. Algorithms compute and organize data facts: Upon receiving the ‘callout package,’ DATAWEAVER’s backend, following Table 1, first computes the relevant statistics following the taxonomy and converts the computed values into a statistical table or template-based data facts, such as “95.24% of the selected data points have the attribute continent = Africa”, or “Gabon is an outlier in lifeExp.”" (p. 6)
"The prompt guides the LLM to first interpret the available datasets using processed information from S2 and then to recommend analyses and visualizations for the selected text." (p. 7)

rq3_entries.value: authors still choose the visual focus and facts, accept or reject prose, direct revisions, and select which generated charts enter the story (PDF pp. 6–7).
quotes: "Users then select desired data facts (S3)." (p. 6)
"Users can decide to accept or reject the generated narrative." (p. 6)
"Eventually, users review the recommended charts and, by clicking an ‘add’ button, select those they wish to incorporate into the canvas as new visualization nodes." (p. 7)

rq3_entries.value: author_raised — the authors identify misinterpretation and bias risks if LLMs take on more interpretive work (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "However, relying on LLMs for more creative tasks increases the risk of misinterpretation and bias." (p. 10)

rq3_entries.value: the user continues to select evidence, judge generated prose, and choose charts; the paper describes no reduction of those responsibilities as competence grows (PDF pp. 6–7).
quotes: "Users click on the statistical table cells or checkboxes to select individual or grouped data facts they want to include from each visualization node." (p. 6)
"Users can decide to accept or reject the generated narrative." (p. 6)
"Users finally review the generated charts and add desired ones as new vis-nodes (S5)." (p. 7)

rq3_entries.value: longitudinal_n_weeks (1; n=5) — five participants used the tool daily during a one-week diary study (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "In the diary study, participants used DATAWEAVER independently over a week, spending 20–30 minutes each day creating visual data stories." (p. 8)

claim_entries.value: the evaluation suggests that the system streamlines data-story authoring while still needing refinement (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "A user evaluation suggests that DATAWEAVER streamlines the data storytelling process while offering opportunities for further refinement." (p. 10)

claim_entries.value: single_condition_usability — the principal evaluation exposed all participants to the system and was followed by a smaller diary component (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "To evaluate the effectiveness and usability of DATAWEAVER and gather valuable feedback, we conducted a two-part evaluation: a focused user study, followed by a longitudinal week-long diary study." (p. 8)

claim_entries.value: 13 — five of the thirteen also entered the diary study (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "We recruited 13 participants (P1–P13) to evaluate DATAWEAVER." (p. 8)
"Five participants took part in a subsequent diary study, each receiving a $60 Amazon gift card." (p. 8)

claim_entries.value: mixed — the sample combined analysts, students, a postdoc, a data coach, and a software manager (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "Participants (6 female, 7 male) self-reported high familiarity with data-driven stories (8 “highly familiar” and 8 “somewhat familiar”), diverse educational backgrounds (6 PhDs, 2 master’s, 4 bachelor’s, 1 other), and job roles (6 data analysts, 4 students, 1 postdoc, 1 data coach, 1 software manager)." (p. 8)

claim_entries.value: descriptive_only — questionnaire distributions, adjusted scores, and averages were reported without inferential tests (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "DATAWEAVER received an average SUS score of 85.77, placing the tool in the “excellent” usability range, with a system utility score of 83.33 [Bro96, BKM09]." (p. 8)

claim_entries.value: one one-hour virtual session for all 13 participants; one week at 20–30 minutes daily for the five diary participants (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "Each received a $20 Amazon gift card for a one-hour virtual session conducted via Google Meet." (p. 8)
"In the diary study, participants used DATAWEAVER independently over a week, spending 20–30 minutes each day creating visual data stories." (p. 8)

claim_entries.value: text-to-visualization performance was inconsistent, and some users found the volume of generated facts overwhelming (PDF p. 9).
quotes: "Text-to-vis composition showed promise but also exhibited inconsistent performance due to data limitation." (p. 9)

"However, the sheer volume of information was overwhelming for some participants (P2, P6, P12) –“There’s just so much going on... it’s hard to quickly find what’s important without getting lost in all the details. [P6]”" (p. 9)

claim_entries.value: the single-condition session and five-person diary support the cautious “suggests” claim about streamlining and refinement needs, but they do not establish comparative performance against another workflow (PDF pp. 8, 10).
quotes: "To evaluate the effectiveness and usability of DATAWEAVER and gather valuable feedback, we conducted a two-part evaluation: a focused user study, followed by a longitudinal week-long diary study." (p. 8)
"A user evaluation suggests that DATAWEAVER streamlines the data storytelling process while offering opportunities for further refinement." (p. 10)

paper_code_entries.value: data-driven storytelling and visualization–text authoring — the work concerns authoring cohesive interactive data narratives (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "Data-driven storytelling has gained prominence in journalism and other data reporting fields." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — the support is designed to help authors complete present-tense storytelling work more efficiently and accurately (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "Leveraging AI and computational algorithms to enhance efficiency and reduce workload, while preserving the user’s ability to control the narrative structure, tone, and depth of insights could foster more meaningful data-driven stories that faithfully reflect both the data and the author’s intent." (p. 10)

paper_code_entries.value: mixed_or_transitioning — evaluated users span professional and student roles, and the text-first path is intended to lower expertise barriers (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "Participants (6 female, 7 male) self-reported high familiarity with data-driven stories (8 “highly familiar” and 8 “somewhat familiar”), diverse educational backgrounds (6 PhDs, 2 master’s, 4 bachelor’s, 1 other), and job roles (6 data analysts, 4 students, 1 postdoc, 1 data coach, 1 software manager)." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: strategy_or_process_gap — authors had difficulty coordinating analysis, visualization creation, and narrative writing in one cohesive workflow (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "Third, the storytelling process involves context-switching between data analysis, visualization creation, and narrative writing, making it challenging to achieve a cohesive and integrated experience." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: process — the evaluation examined efficiency, usability, and the integrated authoring workflow (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "DATAWEAVER’s ease of use, efficiency in data narrative composition, and integrated framework were repeatedly commended." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: artifact — participants assessed the generated facts, narratives, and visualizations (PDF p. 9).
quotes: "All participants appreciated the relevance and utility of the generated facts." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — typed nodes and edges explicitly organize relationships and flow among narrative and visualization components (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "Edges connect these nodes, defining their relationships and flows." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: contingency — the system responds to the person’s current chart selection or selected prose with corresponding facts or charts (PDF pp. 6–7).
quotes: "In each visualization node, users initiate callout interactions to select visual elements, prompting the system to retrieve and dispatch a package with the data subset, metadata, and interaction details." (p. 6)
"The selected text from S1 and attribute names from S2 are fed into the LLM." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: distributed_support — the workflow deliberately distributes work among the author, deterministic algorithms, and an LLM (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "The vis-to-text composition starts with a created visualization and follows an interact-compute-select-generate-revise workflow with users, algorithms, and LLM collaboratively handle respective steps:" (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: llm_or_foundation_model — GPT-4o generates and semantically interprets user-facing content (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "DATAWEAVER’s backend, built with Python Flask, handles server-side logic and API requests, utilizing GPT-4o as its LLM along with other libraries for text generation, semantic parsing, and various computational tasks." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: llm_era — the semantic path explicitly uses GPT-4o (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "DATAWEAVER’s backend, built with Python Flask, handles server-side logic and API requests, utilizing GPT-4o as its LLM along with other libraries for text generation, semantic parsing, and various computational tasks." (p. 5)

limitations: "While the taxonomy covers common chart types and interactions, offering useful guidance for the development of DATAWEAVER, it is not exhaustive." (PDF p. 9)

"Nevertheless, several participants (P3, P6, P11) encountered challenges in generating meaningful visualizations from text, indicating a limitation in the system’s ability to fully capture the user’s narrative intent." (PDF p. 9)
"DATAWEAVER is restricted to performing basic data operations (e.g., filtering) on user-provided or existing datasets." (PDF p. 9)
"The ‘text-driven’ workflow, while reducing the expertise and effort required to create charts, still requires authors’ familiarity with chart interaction and interpretation [FS23]." (PDF p. 10)
"Another key limitation of DATAWEAVER is its primary focus on assembling together data facts while lacking support for higher-level storylines." (PDF p. 10)
"However, relying on LLMs for more creative tasks increases the risk of misinterpretation and bias." (PDF p. 10)
boundary_conditions: "In the Open Authoring Exercise, participants created their own visual data stories using an IMDb movie dataset [IMD24], with the option to start from four preconfigured charts or build from scratch using text linked to the datasets." (PDF p. 8)

"Participants (6 female, 7 male) self-reported high familiarity with data-driven stories (8 “highly familiar” and 8 “somewhat familiar”), diverse educational backgrounds (6 PhDs, 2 master’s, 4 bachelor’s, 1 other), and job roles (6 data analysts, 4 students, 1 postdoc, 1 data coach, 1 software manager)." (PDF p. 8)
"DATAWEAVER is restricted to performing basic data operations (e.g., filtering) on user-provided or existing datasets." (PDF p. 9)
cards.notes: - The evaluation combines a 13-person single-condition usability session with a one-week diary study completed by five participants. `study_design` permits one value, so `single_condition_usability` was used; this loses the distinct longitudinal diary component.
cards.claim: the evaluation suggests that the system streamlines data-story authoring while still needing refinement
